title: Security posture discovery with Montara Financial
summary: Intro discovery on security posture and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer needs SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS-backed encryption. Redwood AE/SE outlined hosted controls and Dedicated/Private options with network isolation and on-prem KMS. Agreed next steps: send security pack, schedule technical deep dive and pilot benchmarks.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connell (Redwood CSM) | Dana Liu (Montara Head of Security), Carlos Ruiz (Platform Eng), Maya Patel (Product), Owen Brooks (DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick run through of Montara's compliance needs, brief on Redwood hosted controls, and deeper notes on Dedicated/Private options and KMS. Agreed next steps and follow-up.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Ethan from Redwood. Priya, Liam here as well. how's folks doing?
[00:08] Dana Liu: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in. We're short on time so we'll try to be concise.
[00:13] Ethan Park: Totally, we'll try to keep it tight. goal today is just to understand your security posture requirements, and talk through Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options and what documents we can share.
[00:24] Carlos Ruiz: Great. Quick background: Montara is migrating a number of customer-facing models into production next quarter. The security bar is SOC2 plus, we also need ISO27001 if possible. We have SSO via Okta and use SAML/SCIM for provisioning. Key concerns are data encryption, auditability, and data residency.
[00:42] Priya Shah: Makes sense. when you say data residency, is that just region bound or do you have stricter on-prem requirements?
[00:48] Carlos Ruiz: Mostly region bound for now, but for a subset of customers we might need private deployment. also retention windows are stricter for certain verticals.
[00:57] Ethan Park: Understood. quick high-level: our Hosted API is SOC2 Type II and we publish an ISO27001 scope for our control plane, we'll share the certs. Hosted supports SSO (SAML + OIDC), SCIM for provisioning, RBAC with roles, and audit logs. For higher isolation we have Dedicated where you get reserved capacity and VPC peering; and Private where the control plane can be customer-managed and you can have on-prem KMS or bring-your-own KMS.
[01:27] Dana Liu: Ok. can you explain encryption at rest and KMS integration details? we need to know if keys are customer-managed.
[01:33] Priya Shah: Yes. For Hosted our default is platform-managed encryption with envelope encryption; we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated we can offer a BYOK flow where keys remain in your cloud KMS - e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS - and Redwood uses the wrapped keys. For Private/on-prem we can integrate with an HSM or your KMS if network allows. There's some additional ops work there.
[01:57] Owen Brooks: When you say "wrap" do you mean the keys never leave customer control? that's pretty important for us.
[02:03] Priya Shah: Correct - with BYOK the root material stays in your KMS, Redwood stores only wrapped-dek material and we never have access to the raw key. For hosted customers that do not opt in, Redwood manages keys. We'll include the KMS integration docs.
[02:18] Maya Patel: On RBAC - can you do fine-grained roles? we want least-privilege so some developers can call the API, Ops can manage deployments, security can view logs only.
[02:28] Priya Shah: Yes, we expose role patterns: admin, deploy, reader, billing, plus custom roles. For Dedicated/Private you can sync groups via SCIM and enforce provisioning through SSO. There are some minor caveats with service accounts and token scoping which we'll document.
[02:45] Carlos Ruiz: Audit logs - how granular are they and what's retention? we need immutable logs for 1 year minimum and export to our SIEM.
[02:53] Ethan Park: Good question. For Hosted we surface audit trails for admin activity, API calls, and model version changes. Logs can be exported via syslog or pushed to S3; retention defaults to 90 days but we have add-ons for longer retention. For Dedicated/Private, you control the log retention and can ship logs directly to your SIEM - most customers do cloudwatch/stackdriver/SPLUNK or direct S3 ingestion. We'll include our audit log schema and sample exports.
[03:22] Dana Liu: Are logs tamper-evident? we need to show integrity.
[03:26] Priya Shah: We provide signed log exports and append-only sequences for audit trails for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we have protections and can provide attestations and hash chains for exported logs on request. We'll include the technical note.
[03:40] Carlos Ruiz: Compliance evidence - will you share SOC2 Type II and ISO certificates and the scope?
[03:46] Liam O'Connell: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II report under an NDA and a high-level ISO27001 certificate; we also have a controls mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to typical customer controls. We'll attach those to the security pack.
[03:58] Owen Brooks: Network isolation - VPC peering vs Private link - can you describe tradeoffs?
[04:05] Priya Shah: VPC peering gives direct network connectivity but costs egress in some clouds. PrivateLink/Private Service Connect is often preferred for simpler routing and stable endpoints; Dedicated supports both and Private can be fully air-gapped if you need on-prem. The ops lift increases as you move left (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private).
[04:25] Maya Patel: About data retention and deletion - how do you handle customer data and logs if we request deletion?
[04:32] Ethan Park: We have data retention policies and an API for data deletion requests. For Hosted, deletion will remove customer prompt history and model cache per SLA; for Dedicated/Private you control retention. We also have options to disable training/retention entirely for sensitive workloads.
[04:47] Dana Liu: Training - just to be clear, hosted models are not used to train Redwood's models with customer data, right?
[04:52] Priya Shah: Correct - we do not use customer prompts to train our public models. We can provide contractual language in the DPA.
[04:59] Carlos Ruiz: On identity, can you integrate with Okta SAML? how about SCIM provisioning to auto-create service accounts?
[05:06] Priya Shah: Yes, Okta SAML is a common integration. SCIM provisioning is supported for user group sync. For service accounts we recommend short-lived tokens and support token rotation. We'll provide a sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping.
[05:21] Owen Brooks: Any certifications around penetration testing or external audits?
[05:25] Liam O'Connell: We conduct annual third-party pen tests and can share a summary. We also have vulnerability disclosure program details.
[05:33] Dana Liu: For high risk customers we might need private deployment. what's the timeline and cost delta for Private?
[05:40] Ethan Park: Private is a longer engagement - typically 3-6 months for on-prem with network/security reviews, deployment, and testing. Dedicated is faster - a few weeks to provision reserved capacity and VPC peering. Cost-wise Private has a setup fee and ongoing license; Dedicated is recurring committed capacity with lower per-token cost than Hosted for heavy workloads. We'll include rough pricing in the follow-up.
[06:03] Carlos Ruiz: For the pilot - we want to run benchmark tests that mimic our peak latencies and retention. would you be able to run a POC against both Hosted and Dedicated so we can compare latency and cost?
[06:15] Priya Shah: Yes, typical approach: run a small pilot on Hosted to validate functional behavior, then run dedicated benchmarks on Dedicated (or Private if you need network isolation) to measure latency and unit cost. We'll ask for a representative prompt set and traffic profile.
[06:31] Maya Patel: Success criteria for us: end-to-end latency under X ms for 95p, auditability with one-year retention, SSO/SCIM working, and documented controls for SOC2/ISO.
[06:43] Ethan Park: Good - we'll capture those as pilot success criteria.
[06:47] Dana Liu: Any gotchas with token-level billing and cost tracking? we need per-team cost attribution.
[06:53] Liam O'Connell: Redwood Console supports token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tagging so you can map usage to teams. For Dedicated, we can export detailed usage files for showback/chargeback.
[07:06] Carlos Ruiz: Data residency - if we go Dedicated in a specific cloud region, can you guarantee that logs and model artifacts stay in that region?
[07:14] Priya Shah: Yes, we can pin deployments to regions and restrict storage to that region for Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we offer region-specific deployments as well. We'll include deployment region options in the pack.
[07:26] Owen Brooks: Regarding legal - do you have standard DPA and security addendum? and what's your incident response / SLA for breaches?
[07:33] Ethan Park: We have a DPA and security addendum. Incident response: we provide incident notifications per SLA and have escalation paths; we'll share our IR playbook summary. For higher-tier SLAs we can agree to additional contractual terms.
[07:49] Dana Liu: Ok. Can you also share your CI/CD pipeline info for model updates - we need to see how model versioning and rollbacks work from an audit perspective?
[07:58] Priya Shah: Absolutely. we have model versioning, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback policies. We emit traces and change logs for model rollouts; we'll include a diagram and the audit events.
[08:12] Carlos Ruiz: Are there known issues with KV cache leakage or prompt caching that could risk data exposure?
[08:19] Priya Shah: We treat KV cache carefully - for Hosted we isolate per-tenant and we have TTLs and options to disable caching for sensitive workloads. For Dedicated/Private you can control caching policies. We'll include recommended configs.
[08:33] Maya Patel: For SAML groups mapping to roles, is that one-to-one or can you do complex mappings?
[08:39] Priya Shah: You can do mapping rules and custom attributes. We'll send sample mapping.
[08:45] Ethan Park: Ok, we're at the technical Q&A portion - anything else?
[08:49] Dana Liu: One last - retention of embeddings and prompts: do you store prompts or embeddings by default?
[08:56] Priya Shah: By default we store for 90 days and use caches to speed responses. We can offer no-retention mode where we do not persist embeddings or prompt history for sensitive customers.
[09:06] Carlos Ruiz: Great. sounds like a plan.
[09:09] Ethan Park: Cool. We'll send the security pack with SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration docs. Priya will follow up for the technical deep dive and we'll set up the pilot scope.
[09:18] Owen Brooks: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:20] Liam O'Connell: Thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with Q&A and small clarifications, timestamps approximate; some transcription errors / names occasionally misrecognized)

[44:12] Ethan Park: quick recap - send security pack, schedule deep dive, customer to share prompts and retention policy.
[44:20] Dana Liu: yep. we'll aim to get those to you by next week.
[44:24] Ethan Park: ok, thanks all.
